notes: Panel 1 is the frame the binary paints *before any command runs* — the startup theme lives or dies there.

Panel 2 opens `/settings`, whose three rows read the live App (`app.theme().name()`, `app.copy_on_select()`), so its text is the visible proof that startup applied the file. The pre-fix binary reports `dark` / `true` here, because nothing but `/settings` and `/reload` ever read the file.
`probe` rows name post-fix behaviour; on the pre-fix binary they report XFAIL instead of failing the run, which is how one scenario documents both sides of the A/B.

The colours behind panel 1 are audited by `scripts/theme_palette_report.py`: the accent/muted/dim tokens are the light-scheme ones, which is only possible if the palette was installed before the first frame.
caption: LUM-1307 — startup application of settings.json (theme + fullscreenCopyOnSelect) in the real pi-rust TUI. Same keys, same prepared HOME (`theme=light`, `fullscreenCopyOnSelect=false`); the only difference is the build. Pre-fix: the first frame is the dark palette and `/settings` reports copy-on-select ON. Post-fix: the first frame carries the stored light palette and `/settings` reports the stored OFF. Real binary + real PTY + pyte VT emulator; nothing mocked.

panels.label: 1. idle 120x34 — the frame painted before any command: stored light palette applied at startup
2. /settings — live rows read the running App: theme and copy-on-select come from the file, not from the built-in defaults
